pr_title: Fix crash on accessing settings after moving game folder
pr_body:
Bit of an unfortunate one, but in theory the usage of `ToLive` should be quite isolated. If anything, i can see us reducing the number of places it is used from the current usages.

Closes #16074

issue_context.title: Crash when accessing settings after moving osu! data location
issue_context.body:
Due to `RealmLive` using an old schema configuration (and not having access to `RealmContextFactory`), the game will crash after accessing settings if the realm file location has changed on disk. This can happen if the user relocates their install.

```csharp
2021-12-13 10:08:10 [error]: An unhandled error has occurred.
2021-12-13 10:08:10 [error]: System.NullReferenceException: Object reference not set to an instance of an object.
2021-12-13 10:08:10 [error]: at osu.Game.Database.RealmLive`1.<>c.<ToString>b__13_0(T i)
2021-12-13 10:08:10 [error]: at osu.Game.Database.RealmLive`1.PerformRead[TReturn](Func`2 perform)
2021-12-13 10:08:10 [error]: at osu.Game.Overlays.Settings.SettingsDropdown`1.<>c.<get_FilterTerms>b__9_0(T i)
2021-12-13 10:08:10 [error]: at System.Linq.Enumerable.SelectEnumerableIterator`2.MoveNext()
2021-12-13 10:08:10 [error]: at System.Linq.Enumerable.ConcatIterator`1.MoveNext()
2021-12-13 10:08:10 [error]: at System.Linq.Enumerable.Any[TSource](IEnumerable`1 source, Func`2 predicate)
2021-12-13 10:08:10 [error]: at osu.Framework.Graphics.Containers.SearchContainer`1.<>c__DisplayClass12_0.<match>b__0(String term)
2021-12-13 10:08:10 [error]: at System.Linq.Enumerable.WhereArrayIterator`1.ToArray()
2021-12-13 10:08:10 [error]: at osu.Framework.Graphics.Containers.SearchContainer`1.match(IFilterable filterable, IEnumerable`1 searchTerms, Boolean searchActive, Boolean nonContiguousMatching)
2021-12-13 10:08:10 [error]: at osu.Framework.Graphics.Containers.SearchContainer`1.match(IFilterable filterable, IEnumerable`1 searchTerms, Boolean searchActive, Boolean nonContiguousMatching)
2021-12-13 10:08:10 [error]: at osu.Framework.Graphics.Containers.SearchContainer`1.<>c__DisplayClass11_0.<performFilter>b__0(IFilterable child)
2021-12-13 10:08:10 [error]: at osu.Framework.Extensions.IEnumerableExtensions.EnumerableExtensions.ForEach[T](IEnumerable`1 collection, Action`1 action)
2021-12-13 10:08:10 [error]: at osu.Framework.Graphics.Containers.SearchContainer`1.performFilter()
2021-12-13 10:08:10 [error]: at osu.Framework.Graphics.Containers.SearchContainer`1.Update()
2021-12-13 10:08:10 [error]: at osu.Framework.Graphics.Drawable.UpdateSubTree()
```

Probable solution is to give `RealmLive` a context factory to retrieve the realm context from, rather than relying on local methods.

review_comments:
I don't feel super sure about this null allowance. Feels like this class is now really two classes at once, because whether the live construction is permissible depends both on the data as well as whether the data was accompanied by a realm factory...

I would actually prefer to have something like the following:
* `RealmLive` always expects to receive a managed object and a realm factory
* `RealmLiveUnmanaged<T> : ILive<T>` is a separate new class which doesn't take a realm factory and only supports reads
* `.ToLiveUnmanaged()` (or `.ToReadOnlyLive()`?) only ever returns the latter, while `.ToLive()` returns the former

The above works as long as it is accepted that an unmanaged object should never get `.ToLive()`d first and only then added to a realm later and start magically working with writes from that point on.

Seems like the interface should give enough leeway to separate the two paths without peppering too many checks everywhere. In a perfect world the unmanaged impl would only implement a `IReadOnlyLive<T>` to avoid having writes throw at runtime but that is probably too much of a muchness at this point.
i'll give this a try. i was considering the same direction but didn't as it's a more time consuming implementation.
Have applied these changes, seems good.

To expand on the the previous point, I'm having a difficult time reviewing these changes because I'm not super sure where it is fine to use `.ToLiveUnmanaged()` and where it is fine to use `.ToLive()`. Looks like the only way to validate this would be to check all references and make sure there are no writes to this `skinInfo`, which is prone to error, and each missed usage is a runtime crash. The compiler could do that for me, but only if `IReadOnlyLive<T>` existed.
Ok, the fact that these usages are only used for equality checks assuages my doubts somewhat. I suppose let's roll with this and see if it backfires, and revisit if it ever does.
